name: CA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 partisan lean in a heavily Democratic North Coast district
Huffman's incumbency and $1.1 million war chest against a challenger with no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Huffman near 96 percent

model.rationale: The district's thirteen-point Democratic lean, Huffman's incumbency and overwhelming financial advantage, and market pricing near 96 percent all point to a comfortable win; with no polling available, the exact margin carries wide uncertainty but the outcome is not in realistic doubt.
model.watch: With no polls and no outside spending on either side, only an unexpected scandal or a late wave of Republican money would meaningfully move the race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's second district runs along the North Coast from the Golden Gate Bridge north, and its electorate leans about thirteen points Democratic. Jared Huffman has held the seat since 2013 and advanced to the general as the incumbent. Republican Robin Littau also advanced but shows no reported fundraising or cash on hand, while Huffman has raised nearly a million dollars and holds just over one million in the bank. No outside groups are spending here, and no public polls have been conducted.

Prediction markets put Huffman's chances around 96 percent, and the underlying fundamentals point the same way: a strongly Democratic electorate, an established incumbent, and a lopsided financial edge. The realistic uncertainty concerns the size of the winning margin rather than who wins, since the race has drawn little independent attention or measurement.
